messages:
sophie (customer): Hey team — we're seeing intermittent invalid JSON from the API when using JSON mode + embeddings endpoint. Happens ~1-2% of requests under load. example response attached, customer is blocked. Correlation: req_id=rid_6e7f1a. Repro steps below.

maya (support): thanks for flagging, sorry about the disruption. Can you paste the exact request (headers + body) and the raw response? Also which model variant + quantization are you using?

sophie (customer): payload: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "mode": "json",
  "model": "rw-instruct-3b:q8_0",
  "input": "generate_metadata",
  "batching": true,
  "cache_prefix": "user:acct-42:prompt:",
  "items": [ {"id":"a"}, {"id":"b"}, {"id":"c"} ]
}
```
raw response (truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: rid_6e7f1a

{"id":"a","output":{"meta": {"user":"acct-42","score":0.92}},"id":"b","output":{"meta": {"user":"acct-42","score":0.86}}
```
Notice the body is not valid JSON — repeated keys and interleaved objects. Happens only when we enable batching + prefix cache = true, otherwise fine.

maya (support): got it. assigning to eng-runtime. @aj can you pick this up? I've uploaded the raw logs to the ticket (link).

aj (eng-runtime): @maya grabbing the logs now. Quick Q: are these requests going through Dedicated pools or Hosted? Any retries configured by client?

sophie (customer): hosted for now. No client retries. Traffic rate ~120 rps, both short and long contexts mixed.

aj (eng-runtime): thanks. initial hunch: KV cache stitching or continuous batching could be merging token streams across shards when a request finishes mid-batch and the runtime reuses an output buffer. Need a minimal repro. @sophie can you try a tiny script that sends 3 parallel requests like your items array but as separate calls (no client-side batching) with the same cache_prefix and see if it reproduces? If yes, that points to prefix key collision + cache write race.

sophie (customer): will try and report back. quick note: reproduces ~40% when I ramp concurrency to 200 rps with batching enabled. single-threaded rarely reproduces.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T17:42:13 started by aj

aj (eng-runtime): pulled a run of logs around rid_6e7f1a. I can see interleaved write ops: two batches A and B share the same output buffer id=obuf-17 and we get writes: write(obuf-17, offset=0, len=512, src=batchA_part1) then write(obuf-17, offset=512, len=512, src=batchB_part1) then a second write from batchA that assumes starting offset 512 — looks like a lost offset update. Attaching snippet: 
```
[2026-03-10T17:40:21Z] obuf-17 write start batchA seq=101 offset=0 len=512
[2026-03-10T17:40:21Z] obuf-17 write start batchB seq=201 offset=0 len=512
[2026-03-10T17:40:21Z] obuf-17 write commit batchB seq=201 wrote=512 new_offset=512
[2026-03-10T17:40:21Z] obuf-17 write commit batchA seq=101 wrote=512 new_offset=512
[2026-03-10T17:40:21Z] obuf-17 write start batchA seq=102 offset=512 len=256
[2026-03-10T17:40:21Z] obuf-17 write start batchB seq=202 offset=512 len=256
```
Looks racy.

tom (eng-ml): could also be KV cache prefix reuse: if we store partial JSON fragments in KV per request using cache key = cache_prefix + item.id, and batching deduplicates prefix writing for similar prefixes, two items with same prefix might get merged. Are customer prefixes globally unique?

aj (eng-runtime): good point. sophie said cache_prefix includes account id but not item id, so keys collide across items in same request. We should be writing per-item keys or include request id suffix. For now we can patch runtime to namespace per-request. But we still see obuf reuse even for unique keys in the logs. Two independent issues might be overlapping: 1) cache key namespace collision -> JSON fragments merged; 2) output buffer reuse without atomic offset updates -> interleaving.

maya (support): what's the remediation for the customer short-term?

aj (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation: disable server-side batching for their account; set batching=false in config or apply a routing policy to force single-request execution path. Also recommend not using a cache_prefix that is shared across items — include item id or set cache_prefix to per-request string. I'll open a hotfix branch to ensure output buffer offset updates are serialized.

sophie (customer): disabling batching reduced the error rate to near-zero. Thanks. We prefer batching for cost reasons — can you ETA for a fix?

aj (eng-runtime): opening GH issue: rw/runtime#4123. Hotfix to avoid obuf reuse in place by next patch (ETA 48h) and a follow-up to change cache key generation in API to include per-request nonce (ETA 7 days). We'll also add a telemetry check for non-JSON responses emitted by JSON mode.

tom (eng-ml): FYI we should warn in docs about using shared cache_prefix across multiple items when using structured output. Also add a validation: if mode==json and items.length>1 and cache_prefix endsWith(':prompt:'), emit a warning in the response headers.

maya (support): i'll relay the mitigation and GH issue to the customer and mark the ticket escalated. Adding a temporary policy to their account to disable batching.

sophie (customer): appreciate the quick triage. Please ping me when the patch is live so we can re-enable batching.

aj (eng-runtime): will do. adding postmortem checklist: reproduce script, logs, obuf trace, kv operations, apply fix, run load test at 200 rps for 1h.

maya (support): marking resolved for now (workaround applied). will reopen when deploy completes. :white_check_mark:
